prompt: Do you have new numbness or reduced feeling between your legs, around your genitals or anus, or where you would sit on a saddle?
message: Numbness in the saddle area can be a sign of cauda equina syndrome, a compression of the nerves at the base of the spine that needs emergency assessment and usually an urgent MRI. Go to an emergency department now.

prompt: Since your back or leg symptoms began, have you had new difficulty passing urine, been unable to pass urine, or lost control of your bladder?
message: New bladder problems with back or leg pain can be a sign of cauda equina syndrome, which needs emergency assessment and usually an urgent MRI. Go to an emergency department now.
locator: Abstract, Results (urinary retention, urinary incontinence) and Conclusion

prompt: Since your back or leg symptoms began, have you lost control of your bowels?
message: New loss of bowel control with back or leg pain can be a sign of cauda equina syndrome, which needs emergency assessment and usually an urgent MRI. Go to an emergency department now.

prompt: Is weakness in your leg or foot getting rapidly worse, or have you developed a foot that drops or slaps when you walk?
message: Severe or progressive weakness needs prompt medical assessment and usually imaging. Contact a doctor today or go to urgent care.

prompt: Do you have any of these with your pain: fever, a history of cancer, unexplained weight loss, a recent significant fall or injury, or a weakened immune system?
message: These can point to a serious underlying cause of back or leg pain that a clinician needs to rule out with an examination and possibly tests. Contact a doctor today or go to urgent care.
locator: Recommendation 3 (serious underlying conditions suspected on history)

prompt: Is your arm, shoulder or neck pain coming with chest pain or pressure, shortness of breath, sweating or feeling sick?
message: Arm or shoulder pain together with chest pain can be a sign of a heart attack. Call an ambulance or go to an emergency department now.
locator: Abstract, Results (chest pain radiating to the arms increases the probability of myocardial infarction)

prompt: Have you recently noticed clumsiness in both hands (for example with buttons, writing or dropping things) or new unsteadiness when walking?
message: Hand clumsiness with walking problems can be a sign of pressure on the spinal cord in the neck (cervical myelopathy). Delayed treatment can cause lasting damage, so see a doctor promptly, today if it is getting worse.
locator: Background (Introduction): manual clumsiness and walking disturbance; delayed treatment may cause irreversible consequences
